sector: A private heritage and memorial keepsake commissioned by a family for a service and to keep afterwards.
founded_place_size: Commissioned 2024 by the Fernwood family, Brattleboro, Vermont, for a service of around sixty people at the Congregational hall.
about: This is a family memorial keepsake for Walter Fernwood, who died at ninety four. It is a book, not a photo album: plates with captions, a contents page, and the granddaughter's eulogy laid out in the middle, alongside a framed page and a small card for mourners to take home. The visual voice is set by two things: the family's wish that nothing be brightened or invented, and the funeral home pieces made for Walter's late wife in 2019, which the new work should sit beside on the shelf.
audience: The family and around sixty mourners aged 45 to 75, most of them reading printed pages rather than screens, many of whom remember the people in the photographs.
price_positioning: Heritage and memorial commission, 300 to 600 dollars. Neither a luxury commemorative volume with gilt and foil, nor a discount photo book with grids and script headings. What the money buys is restraint.

palette.name: Archive Cream
palette.usage: The ground of every piece: each keepsake card, the framed page, every page of the memory book and the share card, as on keepsake_card_2019_press.pdf and framed_page_2019_press.pdf. The only ground and panel colour. Never type.

palette.name: Ink Brown
palette.usage: Names and dates: the guest name on each keepsake card, Walter Fernwood's name and years line and any date, as on keepsake_card_2019_press.pdf and framed_page_2019_press.pdf; may also carry headings, the eulogy, contents and captions. Never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Slate Charcoal
palette.role: mandatory where a relationship line or verse appears
palette.usage: The relationship line on each keepsake card and any verse on the framed page, as on keepsake_card_2019_press.pdf and framed_page_2019_press.pdf; may also carry the eulogy, contents and captions. Never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Mount Grey
palette.role: mandatory as the keyline round the photograph on every keepsake card and on the framed page
palette.usage: The fine keyline round the photograph at the head of each keepsake card and round the framed page's portrait, as on keepsake_card_2019_press.pdf and framed_page_2019_press.pdf; optional round plates in the memory book. Never type, a ground or a panel.

palette.name: Muted Sage
palette.role: mandatory as the point that joins Walter's two years
palette.usage: Only the small point between Walter Fernwood's two years in his name line, per the signature move. Never letters or figures, a ground, a panel, a keyline or a rule.

typography: The Fernwood keepsake runs a four step scale on the two faces the book already uses. Step 01, display and H1, is the share card name line in Familjen Grotesk Light at 64 px on 70 px, Light, caps letterspaced 300 thousandths, centred on one line with the years joined by a small Muted Sage point and set at the foot of the card; inside the book the same line holds at caption scale, 9 pt on 13 pt. Step 02, subheading and H2, is the plate section head in Familjen Grotesk Light caps at 16 pt on 19 pt, tracking 120 thousandths, a size invented because none was stated and set proportionate above the eulogy and below the share card line. Step 03, body, is the eulogy in Adobe Caslon Pro Regular at 12 pt on 18 pt, tracking 0, held to a maximum of 65 characters, with contents entries in the same face at 10 pt on 15 pt. Step 04, fine print, is captions in Familjen Grotesk Light at 9 pt on 13 pt, tracking 30 thousandths, with folios in the same face at 8 pt on 11 pt. The name line is never promoted to a heading at any size, and no script face appears anywhere in the book.
voice: Plain, gentle, unsentimental. Lets the photographs and the family's own words carry. Example line the book would write: The company toured for eleven seasons, and this is his father's hand on the back of the card. No cheerfulness, no exclamation points.
brand_assets_status: There is no brand file. The look is inherited from the funeral home's two 2019 press files (a keepsake card and a framed page) that the family wants matched so the pieces sit together on the shelf, and from the family's own scans, eulogy and typed transcriptions. The funeral home's designer has retired and left only flat press files. Damage in the scans is to be shown honestly, handled by crop and placement rather than painted over.
values: Nothing invented and nothing brightened. Honesty to the photographs as they are, and a keepsake the family can keep editing until the day of the service.

scale.note: The share card name line, and the only place the name runs at this size. It keeps the footer behaviour exactly: centred on one line, caps, the years joined by a small Muted Sage point rather than a rule, sitting at the foot of the card. Inside the book the same line holds at caption scale, 9 pt on 13 pt, the leading set wide by the 300 thousandths. The tracking stays positive here because the signature outranks the usual tight display setting.

Plate section heads and the contents heading. Size invented, none was stated; set proportionate above the 12 pt eulogy and below the share card line. Letterspaced caps, but well short of the 300 thousandths reserved for Walter's name.

scale.sample: He is remembered plainly, in the words his family chose.
scale.note: The eulogy. Contents entries run in the same face at 10 pt on 15 pt.

scale.sample: Family scan, shown as it is and not brightened.
scale.note: Plate captions. Folios run in the same face at 8 pt on 11 pt.

type_system.signature_move: Walter's name and his two years always sit alone at the foot of the page, centred on one line in Familjen Grotesk Light caps letterspaced 300 thousandths of an em, the years joined by a small Muted Sage point rather than a rule. The line is never promoted to a heading, at any size, including the 64 px share card setting.
rules: The name and years line is always at the foot of the page, centred on one line, never a heading.
The two years are joined by a small Muted Sage point, never by a rule and never by a dash.
The name line is always caps letterspaced 300 thousandths of an em, at every size it appears.
Nothing is brightened and nothing is invented; damage in the scans is shown honestly, handled by crop and placement rather than painted over.
The pieces must sit beside the 2019 funeral home keepsake card and framed page on the shelf.
No cheerfulness and no exclamation points.

palette_rules.distribution: Archive Cream is the only ground and panel colour, and photographs sit on it inside their margins. All type sits on Archive Cream, never over a photograph, and is Ink Brown or Slate Charcoal, apart from the Muted Sage point between the years: guest names, Walter Fernwood's name and years line and any date in Ink Brown; relationship lines and verse in Slate Charcoal, as on keepsake_card_2019_press.pdf and framed_page_2019_press.pdf; the eulogy, contents, section heads, captions and folios take either. Mount Grey is for photograph keylines and Muted Sage for the point between the years, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area, never a ground.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph.
palette_rules.forbidden: No gold, gilt, foil or other metallic effect on any type, keyline, rule, panel or icon (price positioning: "Neither a luxury commemorative volume with gilt and foil"), and no colour outside the five palette hexes (#EFE9DC, #3A322A, #4C4A46, #9A948A and #7E8574) for type, keylines, rules, panels or icons.
palette_rules.photography: Photographs keep their own corrected colour: a print's own cast may be corrected toward neutral, but no photograph is brightened, or tinted, toned or recoloured toward a palette colour.
